limitations: Separate diagnostic cohorts; scheduling and batching can change observed operation counts between invocations; one source-bound run per lane is not a statistical performance estimate.

Separate diagnostic cohorts; baseline uses cold actor reads plus summary-event counters, current additionally has hot numeric counters and target dumps. Diagnostic times are not pure timing comparisons.

The common numeric actor field contract and physical formula match and are checked by frozen controls. Scalar events can contain different tree/mark widths; counts do not measure inner rule/call/trie work. Resume callbacks are separate and unavailable in baseline.
Top 40 lists are bounded samples. Exact method deltas use only keys observed in both lanes; missing methods are censored, not zero. All-method counts remain exact aggregate counters.

Packing counts measure certified packed work actually performed, not all work that could be eligible for a future optimization. Untouched counters are nested candidates without a baseline partner or proof they may be skipped.

Stored memberships, protection and coverage partitions are logical output-path×mark units under each lane own policy. The old ANY+alias guard and new STAR/ANY policy differ; do not treat the reason partition as a common-policy counterfactual or mix it with physical row counts.
Outer HARD_TIMEOUT does not erase a complete/accepted run1 census. Baseline Thingsboard SARIF export remains unavailable; no zero finding count or noFN pass is inferred.
Timed reference/current R1 engine times are linked as separate closed cohorts. Work changes are evidence about operation volume, not a timing-causality proof or a matched per-operation CPU estimate.

owasp_regression_assessment.unresolved: The extra timed engine wall time is not explained by these nearly equal outer operation counts.
